days.note: Catch-up starts today. Offer the full amount every feed and let him leave what he does not want. Call the office and ask for a weight-only nurse check before Monday.
Both parents home. Nine feeds, no gap over 3 hours, day or night. Wake him if he sleeps through.
Last full day with both parents home. Weigh naked, same time, same scale. Write the number down for tomorrow.
Appointment 1:15 PM. Bring the question list. Dad back to work from home today.
New schedule starts today. Eight feeds, 75-90 mL each, day anchored at 8:00 AM. Read the 11:00 PM block before tonight.
First night with no alarm after 11:00 PM. Write down the time he actually woke - that number is the whole point of this week.
Second reading. Do not judge the change on one night. Both of you in bed by 11:30 PM again.
Three wake times now. If they cluster, that is his real clock and the 2:30 AM label should move to match it.
Weekend. Same times - his clock does not know it is Saturday. Use the extra hands to bank sleep, not to catch up on chores.
Weekly naked weight, same time and same scale. Compare against last Sunday, not against yesterday.
Three weeks. Check the pumped volumes across the week - if they are trending down, the 6-hour night gap is the cause and it needs a pump at 11:00 PM.
Cord stump should be long gone. If anything is still weeping or smells, call.
Growth spurt window is open - he may want more than 90 for a few days. Give it to him and stop worrying about the ceiling.
Check in on Mom, properly. Ask the question and wait for the real answer.
Add up a full day in Huckleberry. Over 600 mL means eight feeds is working. Under it two days running means go back to nine.
Weekend. Whoever is more wrecked gets the long sleep tonight - swap the 2:30 AM feed if that is Dad.
Weekly naked weight. Expect roughly 150-210 g over the week.
Four weeks. Two weeks of wake times now - if he reliably goes past 3:00 AM, move the float later and stop pretending it is 2:30.
Steady state. This schedule only stays useful if it is still true - change it when it stops being.
One month. Latch is usually stronger by now - test whether he finishes a feed at the breast without the top-up.
If the top-up is getting smaller at the daytime feeds, say so at the next visit. That is the thread that leads out of pumping.
Nothing to change today. Check the diaper counts - 6 wet and 3 dirty is still the floor.
Weekend. Bank sleep.
Weekly naked weight. Five weeks of numbers now - look at the line, not the last point.
Five weeks. If he is taking 90 at every feed and still rooting, it is time to raise the ceiling - ask, do not guess.
Second night feed watch: is he still waking for the 5:00 AM, or is he sleeping past the alarm? That decides what changes next.
Check in on Mom again. Six weeks is where the adrenaline runs out.
Nothing scheduled. If the board and reality disagree, reality is right - edit the board.
Add up a full day again. Compare against the 600 mL floor and against two weeks ago.
Weekend. Same times.
Weekly naked weight.
Six weeks. Rebuild this schedule around who he is now rather than who he was at two weeks. Start with the wake times you wrote down.
